title: Latin Poetry - Meter and Scansion
objectives: Recognize elision and other metrical phenomena

grammar.explanation: The dactylic hexameter is the meter of Latin epic (Virgil, Ovid, Lucretius). Each line has six feet: the first four may be dactyl (-uu) or spondee (--); the fifth is usually dactyl; the sixth is spondee or trochee.

paradigms.name: Hexameter Structure
content: Caesura: usually in foot 3 (penthemimeral) or foot 4 (hephthemimeral)

rules: Elision: final vowel drops before initial vowel
Position: short vowel + two consonants = long
Diaeresis: word end coinciding with foot end

readingPassage.latin: Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris
readingPassage.analysis: DSS | DSS | SP | SP | DAC | SP. Caesura after 'cano' (penthemimeral). Opening spondees give weight and gravity.
